items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: A boy that I had played with at one time in Helvey's band named John L. Henderson

ctx.x: We played a few days in Buffalo and it was at a club called 'Ann Montgomery' that I met a trumpet player called 'Peanuts' Holland who was a blowing cat with a lot of technique and a big sound. Another young musician I met at this same club was a fellow named Willie Smith. I didn't know anything about Jimmie Lunceford, but Charlie Johnson wanted to hire Willie the first night he heard him. I jammed with Willie and Peanuts almost every night.

A boy that I had played with at one time in Helvey's band named John L. Henderson was working in a band at the biggest Negro hotel in Buffalo, so I went to listen to him the night before we were to leave. I had a ball and got so drunk that John L. told me that I could go to sleep in his room as he was also living in the hotel.

I told him that I would have to get up at 10 o'clock the next morning because the band was leaving at 11 a.m. He said that he would have the desk clerk call me at 10 which he did. I was still under the influence of the kickapoo joy juice that I had drunk the night before when I answered the 'phone and instead of getting up then, I lay in the bed to get myself together but went back to slumberland.
